answer: To register, the applicant must prove knowledge of a preimage of a registry-published hash, without revealing the preimage. The preimage is the grove where the identity grows: a random secret generated by the applicant and hashed at enrollment. A proof at the zenith of the protocol convinces the verifier the applicant holds the secret, and the forge of the registry records the hash once, so a second registration with the same hash is rejected and one secret yields exactly one identity.
